newsitem.title: CHINA: China bans serious violators from securities trade.
newsitem.headline: China bans serious violators from securities trade.

text.p: China's securities authorities issued new rules on Tuesday banning people found to have engaged in serious securities irregularities from holding senior positions in the industry or from trading.

The rules, issued by the China Securities Regulatory Commission (CSRC) said that company officials found to have engaged in insider trading and traders found to have manipulated prices will be banned from the industry permanently or for years.
A similar ban will also be imposed on accountants and lawyers found to have collaborated with the violators, the rules, published in the Shanghai Securities News, said.

"Violators found guilty by the CSRC will be banned from assuming senior positions in listed firms or from trading on the securities markets permanently or at least for a few years," the CSRC, China's top securities watchdog, said in the rules.
The rules come into effect immediately, the CSRC said.
The rules are part of a significant tightening of supervision of the securities industry put into force from late last year.
The CSRC has since punished branches of all major Chinese banks and securities houses for irregularities such as use of credit to buy shares on both the primary and secondary markets.

The rules issued on Tuesday said that company officials would be banned from assuming senior positions in the industry for at least three years if found to have been involved in one of the following activities:
- using illegal means to obtain share issues or listings
- trading in their own firms' shares
Serious violators will be banned from the industry for good, the rules said.

Similar punishments also apply to brokers found to have issued false documents, attempting to manipulate the securities markets, engaging in insider trading or using public funds to trade, the rules said.
Accountants and lawyers who make false statements to justify rule violations and engage in insider trading are also liable, the rules said.
"The CSRC will announce the violators who have been banned from the industry, for a period of several years or permanently, through designated newspapers," the rules said.
Listed firms and securities houses must not appoint banned individuals as senior officials, the rules said.
Local securities authorities must cooperate with the central government to ensure that the banned individuals do not continue to operate in the markets, the rules said.
